messages:
incident-bot: 🔔 SEV2 alert: ingress-5xx-rate spike in eastus2 (ALB) detected by observability rule. 5xx rate > 2% for 3m. Paging on-call.
ryan-oncall: I'm on it. what's the scope? any customer pages? :eyes:
maya-support: getting a few DMs from sup-ops: some API customers in EU reporting timeouts and 502s around 09:12-09:30. Support ticket #CS-4821.
sam-sre: looking at metrics — backend 502s correlate with ALB TargetGroup unhealthy flaps in eastus2-a. TargetGroup tg-ingress-eastus2 shows healthcheck fail rate ~60%.
anna-netops: any infra changes in that AZ? I pushed a NAT HA kernel backport to eastus2-a last night but only to a subset of nodes (can check hosts list).
ryan-oncall: can we get a quick curl against the ALB?
sam-sre: `curl -I https://app-eu.redwood.example.com/health` -> `HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway`
sam-sre: tcpdump from an envoy pod shows lots of `RST` from upstream when ALB attempts to keepalive. snippet: ```tcp 172.31.45.9:443 > 10.0.12.45:52344 RST```
anna-netops: that RST pattern matches SNAT port exhaustion symptoms we've seen before when node egress is saturated. checking NAT gateway metrics now.
anna-netops: NAT gateway active connections in eastus2-a spiked to 65k at 09:10, then connection slot thrash.
ryan-oncall: so ALB healthchecks to pods are getting RST because SNAT ephemeral ports are burned -> backends appear down -> ALB removes targets -> 5xx surge. makes sense.
maya-support: customers affected: streaming ingest (EU), latencies for embeddings api. estimated affected requests ~0.9% of global at peak.
sam-sre: immediate mitigation options: 1) shift ALB weight away from eastus2-a via Route53 / weighted policy 2) attach more NAT capacity / add extra egress nodes 3) reduce healthcheck frequency / increase thresholds temporarily 4) failover to eastus1 endpoints
ryan-oncall: do 1 + 3 quickly. Change Route53 weight to move 60% of traffic to eu-west endpoints, and bump ALB healthcheck healthy threshold from 3 -> 5 for 2m.
anna-netops: applying Route53 weighted change now (TTL 30s). will move 60% to eu-west.
anna-netops: Route53 update submitted -> `change-id ZABC123` . propagation should be within TTL.
deploy-bot: automated change: ingress-healthcheck-config updated in infra repo: `healthcheck.interval: 10s -> 15s`, `healthy_threshold: 5`. CI passed, rolling change applied to eastus2 ALB config.
sam-sre: I'm scaling additional egress nodes in eastus2-a and increasing NAT gateway capacity. Started adding 3 more NAT nodes.
alicja-platform: also enabling connection tracking tuning on the node-level (conntrack max increase) as a protective step. Rolling to 30% of nodes first.
ryan-oncall: monitoring. please paste post-change metrics.
anna-netops: Route53 weight shift done. ALB traffic to eastus2 now down ~62% within 45s.
sam-sre: NAT connections dropping from 65k -> 18k after added egress nodes and conntrack bump. TargetGroup healthy count recovering.
maya-support: customer complaints dropping. CS posting update to affected customers now. :white_check_mark:
ryan-oncall: current impact estimate: peak window 09:10-09:32 (22 min), peak 5xx rate ~2.3% for EU traffic, approx 0.9% of global requests affected. No data loss, only transient errors/timeouts. Logging: increased error budget usage for a few customers.
sam-sre: let's keep the longer-term mitigations tracked: - ensure NAT autoscaling threshold lower - move ALB healthchecks to use pod IPs behind local proxies to avoid SNAT for internal checks - consider private ALB with IP target type (no SNAT) - implement e2e test for conntrack exhaustion scenarios
anna-netops: filing infra ticket INFRA-7829 to roll out conntrack tuning clusterwide and NAT autoscale policies.
ryan-oncall: I'm handing off to sam for the postmortem and long-term follow-ups. I'll mark the incident as mitigated.
sam-sre: taking handoff. I'll produce a short postmortem, include timeline, root cause (SNAT/conntrack exhaustion after partial NAT kernel update + healthcheck sensitivity), mitigation steps, and follow-ups.
maya-support: updating CS ticket CS-4821 with mitigation summary + ETA for postmortem.
incident-bot: Incident mitigated at 09:38 UTC. Duration: 26 minutes. Severity: SEV2 -> mitigated.
ryan-oncall: thanks everyone. quick retrospective notes in thread: 1) avoid partial kernel backports on egress nodes during business hours; 2) healthcheck config should tolerate transient SNAT anomalies; 3) Route53 weighted policies proved effective for fast traffic steering.
sam-sre: creating postmortem doc and linking infra ticket and customer impact summary. I'll ping when ready.
alicja-platform: leaving some runbook edits in #eng-runtime after this. will add a short checklist for NAT autoscale.
ryan-oncall: handing oncall to @alicja-platform for overnight watch. all set here. :thumbsup:
